title: Find Usages
summary: Lists every reference to the symbol under the editor caret, in one of four scopes: this bound symbol (default), project, group or everywhere
intro: Read this before changing or removing a symbol, to see every place it is used. With the caret on the symbol choose drag-lint > Find Usages... (Ctrl+Alt+F): by default it lists the usages of exactly that object in this project. drag-lint > Find Usages > This symbol / Project / Group / Everywhere (also on the editor right-click drag-lint submenu) and the scope box on the results panel widen it to every object of the name in the project, the project group or every index; the same list comes from the command line as `drag-lint usages --scope <scope>`.

steps: Needs an index of the project
Put the editor caret on the symbol
drag-lint > Find Usages...
Needs an index of the project
Put the editor caret on the symbol
drag-lint > Find Usages > This symbol
Needs an index of the project
Put the editor caret on the symbol
drag-lint > Find Usages > Project
Needs an index of the project
Put the editor caret on the symbol
drag-lint > Find Usages > Group
Needs an index of the project
Put the editor caret on the symbol
drag-lint > Find Usages > Everywhere

questions.ask: Where is the symbol under my caret used?
Why does Find Usages list only one of several same-named fields?
questions.command: The default scope is This symbol (the object under the caret); pick Project in the panel scope box for every object of the name: drag-lint usages --name <X> --scope project --db <db>
